svg.aria-label: Upper panel: the effective polytropic index read off a standard solar model, against fractional radius. It sits near two in the burning core, rises to a maximum above four near the middle of the radiative interior, then drops to a flat plateau at one and a half through the convection zone. Horizontal lines mark the predicted values three-halves and three. Lower panel: a zoom on the convection-zone base in the logarithmic temperature gradient, showing the model boundary at 0.728 of the solar radius and the helioseismic measurement at 0.7133 with an error bar far smaller than the gap between them.
svg.text: The polytropic index the Sun actually has
Zoom on the base of the convection zone, where that index changes
∇ = d ln T / d ln P
Model: BS2005-AGS,OP. Measurement: Basu & Antia (2004), ApJ 606, L85, rb = (0.7133 ± 0.0005) R from GONG p-mode frequencies.
What the gap indicts is the model's composition and opacity, not hydrostatic equilibrium.
